issues.description: script_content is read without encoding and may fail or corrupt non-ASCII notebooks
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding. Generated pipeline scripts can contain non-ASCII identifiers, docstrings, or user data. On Windows or systems with non-UTF-8 locales this will raise UnicodeDecodeError or silently mangle bytes. Use open(script_path, encoding='utf-8').

issues.description: Entire compiled script is shipped through RPC payload on every compile, inflating responses
issues.detail: script_content is always added to the RPC response even though it is only needed when the user clicks Download. For large pipelines this duplicates the file in memory and over the wire on every compile. Consider a dedicated download endpoint or lazy fetch instead of embedding the full source unconditionally.

issues.description: Download button is rendered even when compiledContent is missing, producing a silent no-op
issues.detail: GetAppIcon is rendered unconditionally in the success branch, but handleDownloadClick early-returns when props.compiledContent is undefined. If the backend response is older or the field is stripped, users see a clickable icon that does nothing with no feedback. Hide the icon when compiledContent is absent.

issues.description: Filename fallback 'pipeline.kale.py' will rarely trigger and may mislead users
issues.detail: split('/').pop() only returns empty/undefined for paths ending in '/'. Compiled paths won't, so the fallback is mostly dead code. More importantly, the real compiledPath may point at a .yaml/.tar.gz artifact while this downloads .py content — the mismatched extension can confuse users.

issues.description: GetAppIcon lacks keyboard accessibility and semantic button role
issues.detail: The icon is given onClick but no role, tabIndex, or keyboard handler, so it cannot be activated via keyboard and is invisible to screen readers as an actionable element. Wrap it in an IconButton or anchor (matching the adjacent <a> styling) to keep accessibility consistent with the rest of the control row.

issues.description: script_content read may fail if compile_pipeline modified or removed script_path
issues.detail: The read happens after kfputils.compile_pipeline. If that step ever cleans up or relocates script_path (some compile flows do), this open() will raise and break compilation entirely for a feature that is purely cosmetic. Read script_content before compile_pipeline, or guard with try/except.

review.summary: The feature is small but introduces a few real concerns. The backend always embeds the full compiled script in the RPC response and reads it with no explicit encoding, which is wasteful and fragile for non-ASCII or large pipelines. On the frontend the download button is rendered even when compiledContent is missing (silent no-op), and the bare icon lacks keyboard/ARIA affordances. Filename derivation and ordering of the file read relative to compile_pipeline are minor robustness issues worth tightening before merge.
